text: I always tell them to optimize for the problems they want to have.
speaker: Scott Belsky
context: Lenny asks Scott about his advice to only build half the features you want to build and how to decide which features to include in an MVP. Scott explains his philosophy of prioritizing the core user journey over additional features. He believes teams should focus on eliminating fundamental barriers that prevent users from experiencing value, rather than building nice-to-have features that users will only request once they're already engaged.
text_ko: 항상 저는 "직면하고 싶은 문제를 기준으로 최적화하라"고 말해요.
text_zh: 我常跟他们说，优化要以你想要面对的问题为目标。
text_es: Siempre les digo que optimicen pensando en los problemas que quieran tener.
key_sentence: optimize for the problems they want to have.
original_text: I always tell them to optimize for the problems they want to have. You want the problem of customers getting through your funnel, feeling successful, using your product and getting value and then saying to you, "Oh, but I need it on this platform, or I need this capability, or I want to be able to share this." I mean you want those problems. So don't do those features now.

vocabulary.definition: To make the best or most effective use of a resource or situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, optimizing often refers to improving processes, systems, or products to enhance performance and efficiency.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'optimize' suggests a focus on improvement, it can imply a trade-off where certain aspects may be sacrificed for greater overall effectiveness.

text: In the first 30 seconds of using a new product, you are lazy, vain, and selfish. You want to get it done super quickly. You want to look good to your colleagues or to your friends.
speaker: Scott Belsky
context: Lenny asks Scott how he built his product sense and what advice he has for younger PMs. Scott explains his framework about the psychology of first-time users, describing what he calls the 'first mile' experience. He argues that understanding human psychology is crucial for product development, particularly recognizing that new users have very specific mental states and low tolerance for friction when they first encounter a product.
text_ko: 새 제품을 처음 써볼 때 초반 30초 동안 사람들은 게으르고, 허영심 있고, 이기적이에요. 가능한 한 빨리 끝내고 싶고, 동료들이나 친구들에게 잘 보이고 싶어해요.
text_zh: 在第一次使用新产品的前30秒，你本能地图省事、爱面子、以自我为先：想赶紧把它搞定，也想在同事或朋友面前留下好印象。
text_es: En los primeros 30 segundos de usar un producto nuevo eres perezoso, quieres quedar bien y actúas de forma egoísta: intentas hacerlo lo más rápido posible para dar buena impresión a tus colegas o amigos.
key_sentence: You are lazy, vain, and selfish when using a new product; avoid learning curves.
original_text: In the first 30 seconds of using a new product, you are lazy, vain, and selfish. You want to get it done super quickly. You want to look good to your colleagues or to your friends. You want to feel successful very quickly by engaging in this product. You don't want to have to watch a tour or read anything, really endure any learning curve whatsoever.

text: If you've lost conviction, you should not be doing what you're doing in the world of entrepreneurship. And I'll tell you, I get different answers. Some people are like, "Oh, Scott, I mean, I have more conviction.
speaker: Scott Belsky
context: Lenny asks about Scott's advice on when founders should quit versus persevere through difficult times. Scott shares his framework for helping founders make this decision by asking them to evaluate their current conviction level compared to when they started. He explains that founders who maintain or increase conviction despite setbacks should continue, while those who have lost belief in their solution should consider pivoting or quitting entirely.
text_ko: 만약 확신(conviction)을 잃었다면, 창업(entrepreneurship) 세계에서 지금 하고 있는 일을 계속하면 안 돼요. 그리고 말씀드리자면, 사람들 답변이 제각각이에요. 어떤 사람들은 "오, 스콧, 제 말은 저는 확신이 더 있어요"라고 하더라고요.
text_zh: 在创业这行，如果你已经失去了信念，那就不该继续做你现在在做的事。我跟你说，我得到的回答各不相同。有些人会说，"哦，Scott，我是说，我现在更有信念了。"
text_es: Si has perdido la convicción, no deberías estar en el mundo del emprendimiento. Y te lo digo: recibo respuestas distintas. Algunos me dicen: "Oh, Scott... quiero decir, tengo más convicción."
key_sentence: If you've lost conviction, you should not be doing what you're doing in the world of entrepreneurship.
original_text: If you've lost conviction, you should not be doing what you're doing in the world of entrepreneurship. And I'll tell you, I get different answers. Some people are like, "Oh, Scott, I mean, I have more conviction. All that I've learned, all the validation I've received from customers, we just haven't figured it out yet. It's driving me crazy."

vocabulary.definition: A firmly held belief or opinion that is often accompanied by a strong sense of certainty.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, conviction refers to the strong belief in one's ideas, products, or strategies, which can inspire confidence among investors, employees, and customers.
vocabulary.nuance: While conviction can be a positive driving force, excessive conviction without evidence can lead to stubbornness or poor decision-making.

vocabulary.definition: The process of starting and operating a new business, typically characterized by innovation and risk-taking.
vocabulary.businessContext: Entrepreneurship is crucial in the business landscape as it drives economic growth, creates jobs, and fosters innovation through the establishment of startups and new ventures.
vocabulary.nuance: Entrepreneurship often implies a willingness to take risks and face challenges, and it is not limited to starting new businesses but also includes scaling and sustaining them.

text: I love bringing design upstream. In fact, that's probably been the cheat code of my career as a product leader, has just been disproportionately empowering design throughout the process.
speaker: Scott Belsky
context: Lenny asks Scott about how he's helping PMs at Adobe leverage AI tools and new ways of working. Scott explains his approach to product development, emphasizing the importance of involving designers earlier in the product development process rather than just at the end for visual execution. He describes this as collapsing traditional organizational boundaries between product management and design functions.
text_ko: 저는 디자인을 초기 단계부터 참여시키는 걸 정말 좋아해요(bringing design upstream). 사실 제품 리더로서 제 커리어에서 그게 거의 치트 코드(cheat code)였어요 — 프로세스 전반에 걸쳐 디자인에 훨씬 더 많은 권한을 실어준 것이죠.
text_zh: 我特别喜欢把设计往前提，提到整个流程的上游去。说实话，这可能就是我作为产品负责人的一个秘诀吧，就是在整个过程中给设计更大的话语权，让它发挥更重要的作用。
text_es: Me encanta meter el diseño desde el principio del proceso. De hecho, esa ha sido probablemente la clave secreta de mi carrera como líder de producto: darle un peso desproporcionadamente grande al diseño en todo el proceso.
key_sentence: Bringing design upstream has been the cheat code of my career as a product leader.

vocabulary.definition: Providing someone with the authority or power to do something, often leading to increased confidence and autonomy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, empowering employees can enhance decision-making capabilities and foster innovation by encouraging initiative and ownership.
vocabulary.nuance: While empowering is generally positive, it should be used carefully to ensure that it does not lead to a lack of accountability.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that is out of proportion or not in balance, often referring to an unequal distribution of effects or resources.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business analysis, one might find that certain groups or sectors are disproportionately affected by market changes or policy decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often carries a critical connotation, suggesting unfairness or imbalance that warrants attention.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to processes or activities that occur earlier in a supply chain or development cycle, often influencing subsequent stages.
vocabulary.businessContext: In product development, bringing design upstream means integrating design considerations at the initial stages to enhance overall product quality.
vocabulary.nuance: While commonly used in supply chain contexts, it can also apply metaphorically to any early-stage influence in a process.

text: If resources are carbs, resourcefulness is like muscle. It stays with you. It makes you stronger, and it helps you have a better intuition and better performance over time.
speaker: Scott Belsky
context: Scott shares his final words of wisdom for product builders, focusing on the current economic environment where companies have fewer resources. He contrasts the recent trend of solving problems by throwing money and headcount at them versus being forced to find more creative, efficient solutions. Scott argues this resource-constrained environment actually creates opportunities for teams to develop stronger problem-solving capabilities.
text_ko: 자원(resources)이 탄수화물(carbs)이라면, 자원 활용 능력(resourcefulness)은 근육 같아요. 한 번 길러지면 계속 남아서 더 강해지고, 시간이 지날수록 직관도 좋아지고 성과도 나아져요.
text_zh: 如果把资源看成碳水（carbs），那应变能力就像肌肉。它会一直陪着你，让你越来越强，长期来看你的直觉更准、表现也更好。
text_es: Si los recursos son carbohidratos, el ingenio (resourcefulness) es como un músculo: se queda contigo, te hace más fuerte y, con el tiempo, mejora tu intuición y tu desempeño.
key_sentence: Resourcefulness brings you further than resources, making you stronger over time.
original_text: If resources are carbs, resourcefulness is like muscle. It stays with you. It makes you stronger, and it helps you have a better intuition and better performance over time. I've always found that resourcefulness brings you further than resources despite the fact that over the last seven to 10 years, we've basically thrown resources at every problem.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to find quick and clever ways to overcome difficulties or solve problems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, resourcefulness is crucial for entrepreneurs and teams to navigate challenges, optimize limited resources, and innovate under pressure.
vocabulary.nuance: While often associated with creativity, resourcefulness implies a practical approach to problem-solving rather than just theoretical ideas.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to understand something instinctively, without the need for conscious reasoning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the corporate world, intuition can guide decision-making processes, especially in uncertain or rapidly changing environments where data may be incomplete.
vocabulary.nuance: Intuition is often seen as a valuable complement to analytical thinking, but relying solely on it can lead to biased decisions.

vocabulary.definition: The act of carrying out or accomplishing a task or function, often measured against established standards or expectations.
vocabulary.businessContext: Performance metrics are critical in evaluating employee effectiveness, project outcomes, and overall organizational success in business environments.
vocabulary.nuance: While performance typically refers to measurable outcomes, it can also encompass qualitative aspects such as teamwork and leadership.

text: Creative professionals can now explore 10X the surface area of possibility. These tools are making them so much more efficient. And some people are like, "Oh my gosh, creative pros are going to be replaced." No. No, no, no. They're not.
speaker: Scott Belsky
context: Lenny asks Scott to talk about what Adobe is working on and Scott explains three waves of transformation driving Adobe's strategy. One key wave is how AI tools are empowering creative professionals rather than replacing them. Scott argues that generative AI allows designers and creatives to explore far more possibilities in the same amount of time, leading to better creative solutions rather than job displacement.
text_ko: 크리에이티브 전문가(creative professionals)들은 이제 가능성의 영역을 10배(10X)나 더 탐색할 수 있어요. 이런 도구들 덕분에 훨씬 더 효율적으로 작업할 수 있게 됐어요. 그런데 어떤 사람들은 "세상에, 크리에이티브 전문가들이 대체될 거야"라고 말하죠. 아니에요. 아니요, 아니요, 아니요. 절대 그렇지 않아요.
text_zh: 现在创意人员可以探索的可能性范围扩大了10X（10倍）。这些工具让他们效率提高了很多。有人就会说：“天啊，创意人员要被取代了。”不会的，绝对不会。
text_es: Los profesionales creativos ahora pueden explorar diez veces más posibilidades (10X). Estas herramientas les hacen mucho más eficientes. Y hay gente que dice: “¡Dios mío, los creativos van a ser reemplazados!” No. No, no, no. No van a ser reemplazados.
key_sentence: Creative pros explore 10X the surface area of possibility, finding 10X better solutions.
original_text: Creative professionals can now explore 10X the surface area of possibility. These tools are making them so much more efficient. And some people are like, "Oh my gosh, creative pros are going to be replaced." No. No, no, no. They're not. They're just going to find 10X better solutions.

vocabulary.definition: Achieving maximum productivity with minimum wasted effort or expense.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, being efficient often refers to optimizing processes, reducing costs, and improving output to enhance overall performance.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'efficient' implies a positive connotation of effectiveness, it can sometimes suggest a lack of flexibility or creativity in problem-solving.

vocabulary.definition: A potential or likelihood of something happening or being true.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and innovation, 'possibility' often refers to the exploration of new ideas, markets, or technologies that could lead to growth and success.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries an optimistic connotation, suggesting hope and opportunity, but can also imply uncertainty or risk.
